1: CareSteps architecture submission. Healthcare Challenge Statement 2: AI Healthier Every Day. Handbook PDF page 37 gives the submission table; page 35 asks for architecture, trust boundaries and key design trade-offs as track guidance. This is a simulated-data prototype. Tool and table counts are read from code. No claim of clinical validation, WCAG conformance or verified live provider is made.
2: Solid arrows are local request/data flow; dashed arrows cross the external service or content admission boundary. Browser-to-routes and routes-to-safety are request/return pairs. Structured forms go through routes and repository validation; the three chat gates run inside run_turn. A blocked safety verdict returns a fixed reply before model access. The output check screens only the live branch, not safety/degraded text. The degraded implementation also uses server-side handlers. SQLite is local to the application host, not a remote database. The external model must implement the OpenAI-compatible chat-completions wire format; no specific vendor is assumed. Education content is admitted at seed time through content_loader; rule JSON is loaded by app/safety/rules.py, rather than downloaded or web-searched per request.
3: Four zones: user device, trusted application, trusted local storage, external inputs. The model has no database credential, arbitrary SQL tool or confirm_draft contract. Server-owned ToolContext carries user_id and session_id; user_id is not a model argument. Some tools write scoped facts and preferences directly. Input schema checks are minimal structural checks, followed by handler/repository checks, not full JSON Schema validation. The signed session cookie is readable, including chat draft values; it provides integrity and not confidentiality. The prototype resolves new sessions to the shared seeded demo profile; it is not a production per-person identity service. Conversation and audit views use session IDs, but this is not proof of full patient isolation. SQLite is not encrypted at rest. Audit redaction is best effort; the store is not cryptographically immutable. Content validation checks source metadata and enabled state, not clinical truth.
4: route() evaluates redflags, boundaries and clarification in order. The first match returns a verdict. emergency, urgent_advice, refuse and clarify all block model access. The rules use text patterns and available structured context; they are not a clinical diagnostic system or a guarantee that all unsafe inputs will be detected. Emergency 995 is the Singapore number already present in the project's configured content, not a new recommendation authored for these slides. Fixed safety payloads and messages return directly. Boundary refusal may offer a question for a doctor or pharmacist. Tests test_emergency_beats_a_medication_request and test_emergency_beats_a_clarification cover priority conflicts.
5: The read example uses the real get_period_stats tool with days=7, rather than the planning guide's non-existent reading_search tool. user_id comes from ToolContext, not model arguments. The handler uses stats.build_period_stats, which reads through the repository and computes period statistics in Python. Results include window, n, coverage, missing days and sufficiency. The model rephrases these and check_output checks the final text. No sample clinical values are invented on this slide. prepare_reading and prepare_medication_report stage drafts. A user action POSTs draft_id to /api/chat/confirm, which calls the UI-only h_confirm_draft. confirm_draft has no model schema and normal dispatch rejects it. Scoped direct-write tools record_barrier, add_question and set_reminder_preference are exceptions to the draft pattern; do not claim that every model-initiated operation needs a second click.
6: A missing configuration or LLM_FORCE_DEGRADED leads to _degraded_turn after safety. A failed provider result before any tools were executed also leads to _degraded_turn. If a provider call fails after tools executed, or the configured round budget is exhausted, the orchestrator builds _fallback_text_from_tools and still returns mode live; that text goes through check_output. This preserves actual mode semantics rather than saying every network failure switches the UI into degraded mode. Executed writes are not rolled back by a later model failure; there is no atomic multi-tool turn. The existing fallback wording can be imprecise for direct-write tools; these slides describe code paths, not a guarantee that every fallback sentence is correct. Direct forms, stats, medication reporting and visit summaries are local. The live mode is not exercised by this artifact preparation.
7: The table names and count are checked by executing SCHEMA in an in-memory SQLite database. This is a responsibility map, not a complete entity-relationship diagram. user_id references connect health/support records to user_profile. medication_item links to care_plan, medication_report links to medication_item, support_action links to barrier_event, and education_fact references education_source. Conversation and audit retain session identifiers. Not every table has an is_simulated column: seeded patient records carry it while education facts and audit use other provenance fields. BP corrections insert a new row and update the old row's superseded_by pointer, preserving the history; this is not an immutable or purely append-only database. The unique dedupe_key avoids repeated logical BP submissions. taken, not_taken and unsure are self-reports; unrecorded is derived from missing reports. Source metadata and team_checked status do not constitute clinical review.
8: The system prompt is caresteps.system.v3 and is provided from app/llm/prompts.py. The initial context is a compact profile orientation plus the last 12 user/assistant conversation messages; tool results are appended as the loop runs. The slide's prompt policy text is a summary, not a verbatim system prompt excerpt. Live numeric grounding scans two- or three-digit integer tokens against numbers collected from tool result data and configured safety constants. It is a heuristic, not comprehensive arithmetic verification. Forbidden phrases are also regex checks. Failed checks replace prose rather than ask the model to repair it. Education citation IDs are populated from retrieve_education results, not extracted from model prose. /trace shows the active contracts, rule metadata, prompt fingerprint, provider status and audit events. Prompt fingerprint is displayed as current configuration; it is not stored on every audit row. Education retrieval is local structured lookup, not a vector database or web search.
9: Automated validation: 170 tests passed using .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q on 16 October 2026. Automated tests do not establish clinical safety, WCAG conformance or live model performance. The current preparation does not contact a live provider or change deployment. Known limits include shared demo profile resolution, signed readable cookie state, no production login/authorization, plain HTTP locally, no database encryption at rest, regex safety/output detection limits, no atomic whole-turn transaction and no hospital/HealthHub/PTEC integration. The model adapter only speaks OpenAI-compatible chat completions; direct Anthropic /messages is not implemented. CodeBuddy/WorkBuddy are development tools, not runtime dependencies. Development proof belongs in submission/tool-evidence, not in an invented runtime cloud component.
